paperTitle: Real-time Hybrid Rendering for Dynamic Reflections
centralContribution: This paper presents a novel real-time hybrid algorithm for rendering dynamic reflections of rigid objects in 3D scenes by combining rasterization, specifically the Screen Space Reflection (SSR) technique, with pure GPU-ray tracing via a deferred rendering pipeline. The core idea involves performing SSR per pixel and using GPU-ray tracing for pixels where SSR fails, thereby significantly improving performance with minimal perceptual quality loss compared to a full ray tracing solution, and demonstrating good scalability for dynamic scenes.

gameObjects.conceptualOrigin: Paper Abstract: Problem and Approach Summary
gameObjects.visualMetaphor: Achieving realistic real-time dynamic reflections in 3D scenes with moving objects is crucial for accurate perception but challenging due to the computational cost of methods like ray tracing. Existing real-time solutions like Screen Space Reflections (SSR) have limitations (e.g., failure for occluded objects or those outside screen space), while cube maps lack physical accuracy. Prior hybrid approaches often only supported static objects or were too demanding for dynamic environments. This paper proposes a novel real-time hybrid algorithm that integrates SSR with pure GPU-ray tracing within a deferred rendering pipeline to overcome these limitations, targeting efficient and high-quality dynamic reflections.
